translations.text: It became clear to the dwellers on earth that the Creator had might and strength when he fixed the regions of the earth in place.
He himself set in place the sun and the moon, the stones and the earth, the stream out into the sea, water and cloud, through the might of his wonders.
The Measurer in his might holds the deep circuit all around in purity, and the whole world.

He himself, God's own Son, can look across the sea and the depths of the ocean, and he can count the showers of rain, every single drop. He himself set the final number of days through his true might.

So the Maker, through the spirit of his glory, arranged and established in six days the regions of the earth, up in the heavens, and the deep sea. Who is there that can fully understand this skill except the eternal God?
He gave out joys, the host and the people: first to Adam, and to that noble race, the first beings, the angels, which afterwards perished.
It seemed to them in their minds that it could be so: that they themselves would be lords of heaven, rulers of glory.

Things went worse for them there when they made their home in hell, one after another, in that terrible cavern. There, in surging fire, they had to wait for bitter sorrow, and could never have the light of the sky in the high-built heavens.
But they had to plunge into the deep surge, down beneath the headlands into the abyssal ground, greedy and ravenous. God alone knows how he had condemned that guilty host!
Then the old one calls out of hell. He speaks his words in an accursed voice, a terrifying voice: "Where has the majesty of the angels gone, which we were meant to have in heaven?
This is a home of darkness, harshly bound with firm fetters of fire. The floor is surging, kindled with poison.
Now the end is not far off, when we must suffer torment together, woe and damnation, and never have the splendour of glory in heaven, the joy of the high seats.

Lo, in better times we once had joys before the Lord, and song in the sky. There the nobles now stand around the Eternal One, heroes around the high throne, praising the Lord in word and deed. And I must wait in torment, in bonds, and because of my pride I can never expect a better home."
Then the terrible spirits answered him, black and sinful, lamenting in their torment: "Through your lie you taught us that we should not obey the Saviour.
"It seemed to you alone that you had power over all, over heaven and earth, that you were holy God, the Creator himself. Now you are one of the wicked, bound fast in a fiery prison."
You thought that in your glory you owned the world and power over all things, and that we angels would share it with you.
Your appearance is terrible! Because of your lies we have all come to this wretched end.
You told us as truth that your son was the Creator of mankind. Now you have more torment!"
So the sinful ones spoke to their chief with deceitful words, with sorrowful speeches. Christ had driven them away and deprived them of joys.
Through pride they had abandoned the Lord's light above, and they had the floors of hell for their hope, a burning evil.
Pale and misshapen, the demons wandered; the ravagers, wretched monsters, moved about throughout that terrible cavern, because of the arrogance they had shown before.
Then the prince of the fiends spoke a second time. He was afraid again [?], now that he had felt the full weight of this torment.
He gave off sparks of fire and venom when he began to speak; that is no fair joy when he drove out words in his torments:
"Once I was a holy angel in heaven, dear to the Lord. I had joy with God, great joy before the Creator, and so did this company.

Then I decided in my mind that I would overthrow the radiance of glory, the Son of the Saviour, and take power over the cities entirely as my own possession, together with this wretched troop that I have led home to hell.
I think that was a clear sign, when I was handed over to damnation, down beneath the headlands into the deep abyss.

Now I have brought you all here as captives, away from your homeland. Here there is no glory of the blessed, no wine-hall of the proud, no joy of the world, no troop of angels, and we may not possess high heaven. This terrible home is set alight with fire. I am at enmity with God.
"Dragons dwell forever at the door of hell, hot in their hearts; they cannot help us.
This [?] home is filled with torment. We have no hiding place where we can conceal ourselves in this deep mist. Here is the hissing of serpents; snakes have made their home here.
This fetter of torment is firmly bound. The fiends are fierce, dim and dark. Here no day shines, no light of the Creator, because of the shadow's gloom.

Once I had power over all glory, before I had to wait in this terrible dwelling, guilty on the floor, for whatever the Lord God will decree for me. Now I have come with a multitude of devils to this dark home.
But I must at times, in flight and on the wing, seek out dwellings, and so must more of you who set in motion the beginning of this pride.

We need not expect that the King of glory will ever grant us a dwelling, a homeland as our possession, as he did before, eternal dominion; the Son of the Ruler has power over all, over glory and over torments.
Therefore I must wander the more widely, abject and wretched, tread the paths of exile, deprived of glory, cut off from blessings, possessing no joy up among the angels,
because I once said that I myself was lord of heaven, ruler of creatures. But it turned out worse for me!"
So the accursed spirit told in words all his hardships together, stained with crimes (a fiery gleam, mingled with venom, stood throughout that terrible cave):
"I am so great in body that I cannot hide in this wide hall, wounded by sins.

Lo, here heat and cold sometimes mingle; sometimes I hear the slaves of hell, a groaning race, lamenting the depths, down beneath the headlands; sometimes naked men fight over serpents. This windy hall is filled with horror all within.
"I may not enjoy a more hopeful home, cities or dwellings, nor may I ever again gaze with my eyes upon the bright creation.
It is the worse for me now that I ever knew the light of glory up among the angels, and song in heaven, where the blessed children have all encircled the Son of the Creator himself with song.
Nor may I harm any of the souls except only those whom he does not wish to have; those I may lead home as captives, bring to the dwelling in the bitter abyss.
We are all unlike the beauty and honour that we once had before in heaven.

Very often we, the children of the Saviour, brought the sound of glory to his bosom, where all of us around him, limbs around the beloved one, raised up the words of songs of praise and spoke them to the Lord.
Now I am stained by my deeds, wounded with sins; now I must bear this fetter of torment burning on my back, hot in hell, bereft of hope."

Then still the keeper of crimes, the terrible monster, spoke many things out of hell, weary from torments. His words flew out in sparks, most like poison, when he drove them out: "Oh, the Lord's majesty! Oh, protector of hosts!
Oh, the Creator's might! Oh, middle-earth!
O day of lights! O joy of God!
Oh, host of angels! Oh, heaven above!
Alas that I am wholly bereft of eternal joy, that I cannot reach heaven with my hands, nor may I look up with my eyes, nor indeed shall I ever hear with my ears the voice of the brightest trumpet!
Because I wanted to drive the Son of the Creator, the Lord, from his throne, and to have power over that joy, glory and bliss for myself, a worse fate befell me there than I could have hoped to have.
Now I am separated from the shining host, led away from the light into this hateful home.
I cannot conceive how I came into it, into this abyssal darkness, stained with wicked sins, cast out from the world.
I know now that he will be wholly bereft of eternal joys who does not think to obey the King of heaven, to please the Measurer.

I must endure this torment, woe and punishments and vengeance, deprived of good things, stained with deeds of old, because I thought to drive the Lord, the Ruler of hosts, from his seat; now, full of sorrowful care, I must set out on paths of exile, on wide journeys."
Then the adversary of God turned back to hell, when he had been humbled; so did his followers, greedy and ravenous, when God drove them into that hot dwelling whose name is hell.
Therefore every man must take care not to anger the Son of the Ruler.
Let him take as an example how the dark fiends all perished through pride.
Let us take as our joy the Lord of hosts, eternal happiness above, the Ruler of angels.
He made it known that he had strength and great might when he drove out that multitude, captives, from the high hall.
Let us remember the holy Lord, eternal in glory, the Lord of all creatures; let us choose for ourselves a home in glory with the King of all kings, who is called Christ;
Let us bear in our breasts blithe thoughts, peace and wisdom; let us remember truth and right when we think to bow before the high throne and ask the Almighty for mercy.
so it is fitting for him who lives here in the joys of the world that his beauty should shine when he afterwards seeks the other life, a land fairer than this earth is;
it is beautiful and delightful there; fruits shine brightly over the cities. There is a broad land, a more hopeful home in the kingdom of heaven, more pleasing to Christ.

Let us turn to where he himself sits, the Ruler of victories, the Lord Saviour, in that precious home. Around that high throne stand the troops of angels and of the blessed, clothed in white; the holy hosts of heaven praise the Lord in words and works.
Their beauty shines with the King of glory for ever and ever.
Then I heard further that the fiend confessed; sin and torments were all very hard for him. In their pride they had forsaken the King of glory.
Soon afterwards they spoke again in other words: "Now it is plain that we sinned up in our homeland. Now we must forever suffer inglorious strife for it through the Lord's might.
Lo, we could have lived in the beauty of glory if we had been willing to obey holy God, and sung to him around his throne a thousand times.
When we were there, we lived in joys and heard the sound of glory, the voice of the trumpet. The bright-voiced chief of the angels arose, and the saints bowed to the noble one;
the eternal Lord arose, radiant with victory, stood over us, and blessed the innocent band every day, and so did his dear Son, the Creator of spirits.
God himself received everyone who came up there and who had believed in him earlier, on earth.
Then it angered [me] that the Lord was strong and firm of mind.
So I began to step forward alone against the angels, and said to them all: 'I can give you lasting counsel, if you will put your trust in my power.
Let us scorn the great Protector, the Ruler of hosts, and take this light of glory for ourselves, all of it as our own. What we have put up with all this time is empty boasting.'
Then we agreed that in this way we would drive the Lord out of that precious home, the King out of his city. It is widely known that we must live on the paths of exile, in grim depths.
God himself keeps the kingdom for himself. He alone is King, who became angry with us: the eternal Lord, the Creator mighty in power.
Now this multitude must lie here in sins, while some rush through the air and fly over the earth. Fire is around every one of them, even when he is up above.
He may never touch the souls that seek their way up there, the blessed ones from the earth. But I may seize the heathen band with my hands and drag them down to the abyss, God's adversaries.
Some must wander through the lands of men and often stir up strife among the peoples of men throughout the world.

Here I must endure everything, mourning the miseries of bitter hostility, sick and full of sorrow, because of what I myself once ruled when I made my home in the heavens, whether the Eternal One will ever grant us a home in the kingdom of heaven, a homeland as our own possession, as he did before."
So God's adversaries lamented, burning hot in hell. God the Saviour had become angry with them because of their wicked words.
So every living person whose heart is good may resolve to put away dangerous thoughts and hateful sins.
Let us always keep in mind the strength of the Creator, and prepare for ourselves a green road up to the angels, where almighty God is.
And the noble Son of God will embrace us if we think about this while we are still on earth, and trust in the Holy One for help.
Then he will not abandon us, but will give us life up among the angels, blessed joy.

The bright one shows us a secure home, bright city walls. Blessed souls, freed from sorrows, shine brightly there, where they may dwell forever after in the city and by the royal throne. Let us make that known!

While we are still alive on earth, let us judge, skilfully unlock what the Ruler has locked away, and understand it spiritually! A thousand angels will come to meet us, if we may go there and have done this beforehand on earth.
So blessed is the person who is always ready to scorn wickedness, please the Creator, and put out sin.
As he himself said: "Righteous men, like the sun, beautifully adorned, will shine in their Father's kingdom, in the protected city."

There the Creator himself, the Father of mankind, will embrace them in peace and lift them up graciously into the light of heaven. There they may live with the King of glory for ever and ever and have the joy of joys with the Lord God, for ever and ever, always without end.
Alas! The accursed one wrathfully resolved that he would not obey the King of heaven, the comforting Father.
The floor seethed with poison, hot beneath the captives. The devils cried out, and throughout the windy hall they lamented their misery, their wickedness and murder.
The multitude there was also set on fire. It was all very harsh. Then their leader, who had come forward on foot there first, was bound fast with fire and flame.

That was a firm punishment; his thegns too had to dwell there in that terrible land, and never again hear the holy joy up in heaven, where they had often had a fair place in service, up among the angels.

Then they were without any good things. They may not live anywhere except [?] in the fire of the abyss and that accursed hall, where misery and weeping are heard far and wide, along with the gnashing of teeth and the lamenting of men.
They have nothing to hope for except cold and fire, woe and torments and a swarm of serpents, dragons and adders, and that dark home.
So anyone who was within twelve miles of hell could hear the gnashing of teeth there, loud and full of grief.
God's adversaries wander through hell, burning above and outside (they suffered misery everywhere), worn out by torments, cut off from glory, robbed of joys.

[?] They had deep designs when they made their home in heaven: they wanted to take the kingdom of the skies away from Christ the Saviour. But he rightly kept the household of heaven and the holy throne.
There is no one so wise or so skilled, or so clever, except God himself, who could describe the light of heaven,
how the radiance shines there all around the Creator's might, throughout that glorious company, where the angels have blessed joy and the saints sing (that is the same) before God.
Then the blessed who come from the earth will bring to his bosom the fragrance of blossoms, delightful plants (those are the words of God),
Then the Father of mankind will embrace them and bless them with his right hand, and lead them to the light, where they will have life forever and ever, a heavenly home, a bright city.
Glory will come to everyone who means to obey the Saviour, and it is well for the one who is able to do so.
That angel was formerly named, called Lucifer, the light-bearer, in days of old in God's kingdom.
Then in glory he started strife, because he wished to have pride.
Then Satan, with dark thoughts, planned to build a high throne in heaven, up beside the Eternal One. He was their lord, the originator of evil.

Afterward he regretted it, when he had to sink down to hell, and his retinue with him, sliding into humiliation and the Saviour's hostility, and never afterward could they look upon the eternal face, world without end.
Then terror came upon them, a din before the Judge, when he broke and bent down the door in hell. Joy came to people when they saw the Saviour's head.

Then it was [?] for the terrible ones we named before. They were all frightened with terror, and widely throughout the windy hall they lamented in words: "This is violent, now that this storm has come, a thane with a troop, the Prince of angels.
Before him travels a fairer light than we ever saw with our eyes before, except when we were up above with the angels.
Now through the power of his glory he means to overthrow all our torments. Now that this terror has come, this din before the Lord, this dreary band must soon suffer horribly.
It is the very Son of the Ruler, the Lord of angels. He means to lead souls up from here, and afterward we must forever suffer humiliation for that act of wrath."
Then the Lord went down to hell by his might for the sake of the children of men; he wished to lead forth a great number of people, many thousands, up to their homeland.
Then came the sound of angels, a din at dawn; the Lord himself had overcome the fiend. The feud was still out in the open in the hours before dawn, when the terror came.
Then he let the blessed souls go up, the kin of Adam, but Eve was not yet allowed to look upon glory until she had spoken these words:
"I angered you once, eternal Lord, when Adam and I ate apples because of the serpent's malice, as we never should have.
The terrible one, who now burns forever in bonds, taught us that we would have glory, a holy home, heaven in our power.
When we believed the words of the accursed one, we took with our hands the bright fruits on the holy tree;
we were bitterly repaid for that when we had to go into this hot pit and afterward live here for a number of winters, many thousands, fiercely burned.
"Now I implore you, Guardian of the heavenly kingdom, by the household that you led here, the troops of angels, that I may be able and allowed to go up from here with my kin."
And after three nights the Saviour's thane came home to hell; [he] is now held strongly in fetters, weary with torments, because the King of glory became angry with him for his arrogance.
You told us truly that God himself would bring light to the home of hell's inhabitants.
Then each one rose, sat up on his arm and leaned on his hand. Though the horror of hell seemed dreadful, they were all glad in their sins that the noble Lord wished to come to hell to help them."
Then she reached out her hands to the King of heaven and begged the Creator for mercy through Mary: "Lo, Lord, you were born from my daughter into the world to help mankind.
Now it is plain that you are God himself and the eternal origin of all created things."

Then the eternal Lord let them go up. In his glory he had fastened fetters of torment on the fiends, and he shoved them further into that deep darkness, tightly bent down, where Satan now speaks darkly, the wretched monster, and the terrible ones with him, weary with torments.
They may not have the light of glory at all, only the depths of hell, and they may never again hope for a return.

The Lord God had become angry with them. He gave them a fetter of torment as their dreadful possession, and the horror of terror, the dim and dark shadow of death, the hot depths of hell, the horror of death.
Oh, that was a fair thing, that the company came up to the homeland, and the Eternal One with them, the Lord of mankind, into the glorious city!
The holy prophets, the kin of Abraham, lifted him up with them by their hands to the homeland.
Then the Lord himself had overcome death and put the fiend to flight, just as prophets said in days of old that he would.
All this was done in the hours before dawn, before daybreak: the din came, loud from the heavens, when he broke open hell's door and bent it down. Bones withered when they saw so bright a light.
Then the firstborn Son of God sat with the host and said in true words: "Wise spirits, I made you through my might, Adam first and the noble woman.

Then, by God's will, they had forty children, so that from them multitudes sprang up across the earth and were allowed to live for many winters, men in their homeland, until it happened again that the fiend drove them away once more through sins; he is hostile everywhere.
"In paradise I newly planted a tree with branches, so that its boughs bore apples high up, and you two ate the bright fruits, as the baleful one told you to, the servant of hell.
You had the hot abyss because you two neglected the Saviour's word and ate the dreadful thing [?]. The terrible one was there before you, the one who gave you both baleful thoughts.
Then I was grieved that my handiwork suffered the fetters of the prison.
There was then no measure of men, no might of angels, no work of prophets and no wisdom of men that could help you, except God the Saviour, who had earlier set that punishment as retribution.
He travelled to earth from above, from his homeland, by way of a virgin's state, and on earth he endured many torments and great injury.
Many men, counsellors of the kingdom, plotted around me day and night over how they might inflict the pain of death on me.
Then the appointed span of time had passed: by the count of winters I had been in the world thirty-three years before I suffered.

I was mindful of the multitude in my home [?] long since, and so I led them home from captivity up to the homeland, so that they shall possess the Lord's glories and the majesty of the host. They dwell in joys and have the bliss of glory a thousandfold."
"I interceded for you when men pierced me on the cross, with spears on the gallows. The young man struck there, and I came back up to eternal joys, to the holy Lord."
So the Guardian of glory, the Ruler of mankind, spoke in words, early on the morning on which the Lord God arose from death.
No stone was fastened so strongly, even if it were bound all round with iron, that it could withstand that great power. But he went out, the Lord of angels,

[?] in the stronghold, and he commanded the all-bright angels to fetch the eleven disciples, and above all commanded them to tell Simon Peter that he might see God in Galilee, eternal and steadfast, as he had before.

Then I heard that the disciples all went together to Galilee. They had the glory of the Spirit. They recognized the holy Son of God when they saw where the Son of the Ruler stood up there, the eternal Lord, God in Galilee.
Then the disciples all ran there, to where the Eternal One was.
They fell to the ground and bowed down at his feet; they thanked their Prince that it had so happened that they saw the Creator of the angels.
Then at once Simon Peter spoke: "Is this you, Lord, honoured with glory?
We saw you at one time when heathens laid you in hateful bonds with their hands. They may rue it when they see the end again."

Some could not grasp in their minds that it was the dear one. One of them, named Didymus, could not until he took hold of the Saviour himself with his hands by the side, where he had shed his blood. The baths of baptism fell to the earth.
Fair was that undertaking which the noble Lord, our Prince, suffered.
He mounted the tree and shed his blood, God on the gallows, through the might of his spirit.

Therefore people must at all times give thanks to the Lord in deeds and works, because he led us home from captivity up to the homeland, where we shall possess the Lord's glories and may dwell in joys.
The bright light of glory is opened to us, to whoever thinks rightly.

Then the eternal Lord was on earth for forty days, followed by the people and made known to mankind, before he, the Founder of the city's people, chose to bring the holy spirit into the glorious creation, to the kingdom of heaven.

The Creator of angels, the Ruler of hosts, ascended up into the heavens. Then a sound came in the clouds, holy, from the heavens. With it was the hand of God, which received the noble Lord, and the Prince of the heavens led him forth to the holy home.

Troops of angels flew around him by thousands. When this had happened, the saving Christ also said that ten nights after this he would strengthen the twelve apostles, his disciples, with the gift of his spirit.
The living God had then set countless souls in their place. Then Judas was gone, he who had earlier sold the radiant one, the Lord Saviour, as [?];
That deed did him no good, when he sold the Son of the Ruler for a treasure of silver; the wretched monster paid him back darkly for it inside hell.
Now the Son sits at his Father's right hand; every day the Lord of hosts gives help and salvation to the children of men throughout the world.
It is known to many that he alone is the maker and ruler of all creatures through the power of his glory.
The holy angel [?] sits in the heavens, the Ruler with the prophets. The Son of glory has his own seat, enclosed by heaven.

He invites us there to the light through his healing, where we ourselves may sit with the Lord, up with the angels, and have that same light, where his holy household now dwells and lives in joys, where the splendour of glory is brightly revealed.
Let us take good thought that we eagerly obey the Saviour and please Christ. There is a more glorious life there than we could ever gain on earth.
The glorious Prince, almighty God, the Lord himself, has now appointed a meeting with us on Judgment Day.
He will command archangels with loud voices to blow trumpets over the dwellings of cities throughout the corners of the earth.
Then men will awaken out of this earth; the dead will arise from the dust through the Lord's might.
That will be the longest of days, and the greatest of din will be heard loudly, when the Saviour comes, when the Ruler travels with the clouds into this world.
He will then separate the beautiful and the unclean onto two sides, the good and the evil.
The righteous will ascend to rest with the Guardian of the heavens at his right hand.
Then those who may go into the city, into God's kingdom, will be joyful, and the King of all creatures will bless them with his right hand and call out over them all: "You are welcome!
Go into the light of glory, to the kingdom of heaven, where you will have eternal rest forever and ever."
Then the damned, those who sinned, will stand there, trembling over when the Son of God will judge them according to the sum of their deeds.

They expect that they may go to the glorious city, up to the angels, as others did. But the eternal Lord will speak to them; he said before all: "Go down now, you accursed ones, into the house of torment, in great haste. Now I do not know you."

Immediately after those words the accursed spirits, the captives of hell, will glide in throngs by the thousand and lead them there into that den of criminals, shove them to the bottom into that narrow torment,
and never afterwards may they ever come up from there, but there they must endure wretched punishment, fetters and prison, and suffer the cold deep abyss and the devil's talk:

how the black torment-slayers often cast it at them in reproach, how the fiends charge them with hostility and sin, in that they had often forgotten the noble Lord, the eternal sole Ruler, whom they should have had as their hope.
Come, let us consider, throughout this world, that we should begin to obey the Saviour!
Let us eagerly, through God's grace, keep in mind the glory of the spirit, how the blessed sit up there themselves in heaven, the sons of the Saviour!

There is a golden gate adorned with gems, wreathed with joys, for those who are allowed to go into the light of glory, into God's kingdom; and around the walls the spirits of angels and the blessed souls who journey from here shine beautifully.
There martyrs please the Creator and praise the High Father with holy voices, the King in the city.
They all say this: "You are the protector of men and heaven's judge, origin of angels, and you have led earth's offspring up to this blessed home."
So the thanes around their Prince praise the Guardian of glory with words. There is great majesty there and song at the throne; the King himself is there, Lord of all, in that eternal creation.
That is the Lord who suffered death for us, the Prince of angels.
Likewise he fasted forty days, the Creator of mankind, through the abundance of his mercies.
Then it befell the accursed one, who had earlier been cast out of the heavens so that he plunged into hell, when he tempted the King of all creatures.
He brought broad stones to his lap and told him to make loaves from them because of his hunger: "if you have so much power."

Then the eternal Lord answered him: "Did you think, accursed one, that it was not written: except me alone [?]... but you have established [?] ... the possessor of victory, light for the living, reward without end in the kingdom of heaven, holy joys."

Then the terrible one took him in his hands in mockery and lifted him onto his shoulders, the harmful spirit of evil [?], and climbed onto a mountain and set the Lord Saviour down on the hill: "Look now far and wide over the land-dwellers.

I will give you people and land to rule as you choose. Take from me here the city and the broad dwelling into your power, of the kingdom of the heavens [?], if you are the rightful king of angels and men, as you claimed before."
Then the eternal Lord answered him: "Depart, accursed one, into the pit of torment, Satan yourself. Torment is appointed for you, made ready to meet you, and not God's kingdom.

But I command you by the highest power that you offer no hope to the dwellers in hell. Instead you may tell them the greatest of sorrows: that you met the Lord of all creatures, the King of mankind. Turn yourself backward!
Know also, accursed one, how wide and broad the dreary hall of hell is, and measure it with your hands.
Grasp at the bottom, and go on like that until you know the whole circuit of it. First measure from the top down to the bottom, and how broad the black vapour is.
Then you will know all the more clearly that you strove against God, once you have measured with your hands how high and deep hell is within, that grim grave-house.
Go to it quickly, so that before two hours have passed you will have measured the marked-out house."
Then vengeance pressed close upon the accursed one.
Satan himself ran and fell into the torment, the wretched monster. At times he measured woe and torments with his palms. At times the dark one lay [?] ... against the hateful one [?].
At times he saw captives lying in hell. At times a cry went up when they saw the terrible one with their eyes.
God's adversary, the pale spirit of evil, had [?] struggled on until he stood on the bottom.
Then it seemed to him that from there to the door of hell was a hundred thousand miles by measure, as the Mighty One had commanded him to measure out the torment by his own skill.
Then he realised that he was standing on the bottom.
The false creature, terrible to look on, gazed with his eyes through that hateful pit, until the dreadful terror of the multitude of devils rose up.
Then in the torments the accursed spirits began to speak in words and say: "Lo, so be you now in evil! You would not do good before!"
